approach: Create docs/spec.toml as an array of [[requirement]] tables (id, statement, kind, status, optional supersedes, sources = [{heading, quote}]) plus [[open_question]] tables with at least two sourced quotes each. Create xtask/tests/spec.rs with a pure `check(spec_text, brief_text) -> Vec<String>` function. One test runs it on the real files and expects no problems. Other tests mutate the parsed spec in memory (bad quote, duplicate id, dangling supersedes, no sources) and expect each to be flagged. A coverage test counts requirements by source heading for R1–R8, Phases 1–6, section 10 and addenda 3C, 4A, 5A, 7A. xtask already has `toml` and `serde` as dev-dependencies, so Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock likely need no change; the producer confirms with `cargo test --locked`. Key trap: BRIEF.md is athena-readonly, so the M19 scan in policy.rs skips it, but it does scan docs/spec.toml. Several Olympus lines contain words M19 bans (the Hermes row and §8 'handoffs', 'Context and handoff failures', and the 2A and 'brain' addenda's references to the party that runs Athena and its sandbox). Quotes must therefore be substrings that stop short of those words, and the statements must not describe who runs Athena or where. Then record the format in docs/decisions.md as D111, add a CHANGELOG entry, a new enforcement.md row naming the spec tests, and an ontology term 'spec'.

decisions.choice: TOML with [[requirement]] and [[open_question]] tables, parsed by the existing `toml` crate
decisions.reason: The repository already uses TOML for data (docs/ontology.toml, which has its own checker). A maintained crate is already a dev-dependency (buy-first). The policy test treats TOML as data. Multi-line quotes and nested source tables are easy to check.

rejected.why: It needs a hand-written parser, and fields and quotes would be fragile to extract.
No comments, awkward multi-line text, and noisy diffs for a document that Sri reads and approves.
Implicit typing, and the YAML crates are less maintained. Policy already treats YAML as an exception.

decisions.choice: Source heading is the exact BRIEF.md heading text; for addenda items, `<heading> › <item label>` such as `2026-10-17: Olympus › 3C`. The checker requires the part before ' › ' to be a real heading line in BRIEF.md and the quote to appear after the '# Project Olympus' line.
decisions.reason: This lets the coverage test count by heading and ensures the quote comes from the Olympus layer only. Addenda items share one heading, so the label is needed.

rejected.why: They go stale as BRIEF.md grows by appending.

decisions.choice: Quote check: collapse all whitespace runs to one space on both sides and test substring containment. Quotes are partial sentences chosen to avoid the words M19 bans.
decisions.reason: This matches the stated criterion, and the policy test keeps passing.

rejected.why: They would include banned words in the hand-off and operator lines.

rejected.option: Editing policy.rs to exempt the spec
rejected.why: It weakens a protected check, and criterion 5 forbids it.

decisions.choice: Open questions are recorded as quotes only (`id`, `question`, `sources` of at least 2, no resolution field). Candidates to confirm against the text: 'I'm not sold the API surface should be considered settled' against the treatment of the API as settled in earlier parts of the Athena brief or the Olympus layer; 'reconsider its own design every few jobs' leaves the cadence open; 5A 'No formal ontology for now' leaves open when a formal one would be adopted.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 says to record, not resolve. The producer must pick at least one pair where both quotes really exist in BRIEF.md.

rejected.option: Resolving the conflict in a requirement
rejected.why: This is Sri's call, and criterion 4 says it is not resolved.

decisions.choice: Add a short 'spec' term to docs/ontology.toml with a misread, sources ["docs/spec.toml", "D111"] and a relation to an existing term.
decisions.reason: It is listed as a deliverable and follows 5A (a term is added when it causes a misread). The term is needed because 'spec' is easily confused with the Athena brief or design docs. The existing ontology checker validates that the sources exist.

rejected.why: It is a listed deliverable, and the word 'spec' is ambiguous.

files.purpose: The cohesive Olympus requirements layer: requirements with id, statement, kind, status and sourced quotes, plus open questions.
The checker (`check`) and its tests: the real spec, four negative cases, coverage by heading, schema, and open questions.
Under Unreleased/Added, record the spec and its checker.
Append D111: the spec format and the choice of TOML, with alternatives (Markdown with ids, JSON, YAML), tradeoff, reversal cost and provenance.
Add the next M row for the spec rule, naming real test functions in xtask/tests/spec.rs (checked by M24).
Add the term 'spec', with its misread, sources docs/spec.toml and D111, and a relation to an existing term.
Only if needed: `toml` and `serde` are already dev-dependencies, so likely unchanged. Add a dependency only if the producer needs one, and say so.
Only changes if xtask/Cargo.toml changes. Run with --locked to confirm.

steps: Re-read BRIEF.md lines 550–1013 and list every requirement-bearing sentence with its heading. Merge duplicates across sections into one requirement with several sources.

Write docs/spec.toml: header comment explaining the format, then [[requirement]] tables (id like OLY-001, statement, kind, status, optional supersedes, sources with heading and quote) and [[open_question]] tables. Avoid M19's banned words and fragments in quotes and statements.

Write xtask/tests/spec.rs: serde structs with deny_unknown_fields, a whitespace-collapsing `normalize`, a `headings(brief)` helper, and `check(spec, brief) -> Vec<String>` covering quotes, unique ids, supersedes targets, non-empty sources, enum values and the Olympus-only restriction.

Add tests: the real spec passes; negative cases for (a) quote not verbatim, (b) duplicate id, (c) dangling supersedes, (d) no sources; coverage by heading for R1–R8, Phases 1–6, section 10, 3C, 4A, 5A and 7A, plus a negative that removes one group; schema and merged-duplicates check; open questions with two verbatim quotes each.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`, then fix any quote mismatches and any policy.rs hits.
Add D111 to docs/decisions.md, the CHANGELOG entry, the enforcement.md row (after finding the last M number), and the ontology term. Check that the ontology test and the enforcement-map test pass.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. Touch xtask/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock only if a dependency is genuinely needed.

risks.risk: Quotes in docs/spec.toml contain the word 'handoffs' or a reference to the party running Athena or its sandbox, which fails M19 in policy.rs.
risks.mitigation: Choose quotes as substrings that stop short of banned words. The producer runs `cargo test -p xtask` and fixes policy.rs hits before finishing. Statements describe Olympus roles only (e.g. 'Hermes coordinates execution'), never who runs Athena or where. The 2A and 'brain' addenda are covered by quotes that avoid those words, or are left as owner-side and out of scope.

risks.risk: A quote differs from BRIEF.md by a character, such as a dash or bullet, or by line wrapping.
risks.mitigation: Make the quote check collapse whitespace on both sides. Use straight text copied from the lines read. Avoid quoting across line breaks that include list markers or Markdown bullets, and keep em dashes exact.

risks.risk: Coverage is incomplete, a probable cause of the earlier rejection.
risks.mitigation: Write the coverage test from an explicit key list, with a negative test that removes a group. The producer works through BRIEF.md lines 550–1013 section by section.

risks.risk: Scope creep into the earlier Athena brief or into readers and prompts.
risks.mitigation: Cite only Olympus-layer text (after '# Project Olympus'), and have the checker enforce that. No Athena-brief parts are specified.

risks.risk: Clippy or fmt failures in the new test file.
risks.mitigation: Use `unwrap` or `expect` only in the same way policy.rs does. Check against the workspace lints, and run clippy and fmt before finishing.

demonstrations.method: Integration test in xtask/tests/spec.rs parses the real docs/spec.toml and BRIEF.md and runs `check`. Four negative tests each mutate the parsed spec in memory (altered quote, duplicated id, supersedes pointing at a missing id, emptied sources) and assert that `check` reports the specific problem.
demonstrations.observes: All tests in xtask pass. The real spec yields zero problems, and each of the four mutations yields a problem naming its cause.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the checker did not test containment after whitespace collapse, uniqueness of ids, existence of supersedes targets, or a non-empty sources list, the matching negative test would pass the mutated spec and fail on its assertion that a problem is reported.

demonstrations.method: The coverage test groups requirements by each source's heading (and item label for addenda) and asserts a count of at least 1 for each required key (R1–R8, Phase 1–6 with their Acceptance lines, '10. Final system acceptance', and 3C, 4A, 5A, 7A). A second case removes one group's requirements in memory and expects the failure.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes on the real spec. The in-memory removal makes it report the missing key.
demonstrations.fails_without: With a requirement missing for any one of R1–R8, Phases 1–6, section 10, 3C, 4A, 5A or 7A, the coverage test fails and names the missing heading.

demonstrations.method: The schema test in the same file deserialises every requirement with serde (deny_unknown_fields) and validates the enums and non-empty fields. Coverage also requires sources under the Vision, Governing philosophy, and sections 1–9 headings. The merging of duplicates is reviewed by reading git diff and docs/spec.toml, with ids unique and cross-section duplicates carrying several sources.
demonstrations.observes: All requirements validate. Each section 1–10 heading, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda appear among source headings.
demonstrations.fails_without: A requirement missing an id, statement, a kind outside {goal, requirement, constraint, acceptance}, a status outside {active, superseded} or sources, or a source missing a heading or quote, makes the schema test fail. A vision or philosophy sentence left out would show as a missing heading in the coverage test.

demonstrations.method: The test asserts at least one [[open_question]], each with at least two sources whose quotes are verbatim in BRIEF.md (same containment check), and no field that resolves it.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes, and the spec's open question shows both of Sri's quoted statements.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no open question, or one with fewer than two sources, or a quote not found in BRIEF.md, the open-question test fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole xtask suite, which includes the unchanged xtask/tests/policy.rs. docs/spec.toml is tracked or visible to its scan in the working tree used by the verifier. If the file is only untracked, the verifier checks the same text with `git diff` once it is staged.
demonstrations.observes: `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` and the other policy tests pass with docs/spec.toml present. policy.rs is unmodified, as `git diff` shows.
demonstrations.fails_without: If docs/spec.toml included any of the words or path fragments M19 bans (through a quote or a statement), `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` in policy.rs would fail and list file:line.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. The new test file must use no unwrap or expect that the workspace lints forbid, and must follow the existing style in policy.rs.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit zero. The tests include the enforcement-map test, which finds every test name in the new enforcement row.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting, lint or test failure would make one of the three commands exit non-zero.

demonstrations.method: Read `git diff` for CHANGELOG.md (an entry under Unreleased/Added for docs/spec.toml and its checker), docs/decisions.md (D111: case, decision, alternatives Markdown with ids, JSON, YAML, tradeoff, reversal cost, provenance), docs/enforcement.md, docs/ontology.toml and the file list. Confirm no changes under crates/ and no changes to any prompt or reader. The `cargo test` run covers the ontology and enforcement-map checks.
demonstrations.observes: The changed files are only the deliverables. The spec covers the Olympus layer alone and no earlier Athena brief parts.
demonstrations.fails_without: Not behavior. Without the entries, reading the diff would show no CHANGELOG or D111 text.

open_questions: Which exact pair of Sri's statements best forms the open question. The producer must re-read BRIEF.md, take only pairs that exist in it, and not rely on my candidate list.
Whether the 2026-10-18 addendum on the history exemption should be covered. The brief names only 2026-10-17 addenda, so the plan leaves it out unless it states a standing requirement.
Whether the enforcement.md rows after M30 continue past M31. The Grep output omitted long lines, so the producer must find the last M number before adding a row.

Whether docs/spec.toml is inside the file set M19 scans when the verifier runs `cargo test`. That depends on git tracking, since athena_files uses `git ls-files`. Either way, the producer should keep the file free of banned words.
